title: Restriction and finite-stratum detection of the adic completion unit
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], put $R_n=(A/I^n)_X$ and $B_X=\varprojlim_nR_n$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $u$ be either a locally closed stratum immersion $S\to X$, restriction to a pro-etale site object $U\to X$, or a composite of these two restrictions. For each restricted scheme $Y=S$ or $U$, put $B_Y=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_Y$. Identify coefficient sheaves by the maps induced from the quotient projections. Then $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_S$ (respectively $B_U$), module pullback is exact, and there are canonical isomorphisms
$$u^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{B_X}R_n)\cong u^{-1}K\otimes^L_{B_S}(A/I^n)_S,$$
with $S$ replaced by $U$ as necessary. They commute with quotient transitions and normalization maps. For the specified strict quotient tower let $\eta_K:K\to R\lim_n(K\otimes^L_{B_X}R_n)$ be the quotient completion unit [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Its inverse image identifies with $\eta_{u^{-1}K}$, including the map from $u^{-1}K$. Intrinsic derived $I$-completeness [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is preserved by these restrictions. For any finite stratification of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification] and chosen pro-etale covering of each stratum, $K$ is intrinsically complete if and only if all its restrictions to those covering members are intrinsically complete.

proof.text: For each restriction $u:Y\to X$, the canonical constant-ring maps identify $u^{-1}R_n$ with $(A/I^n)_Y$, since every $A/I^n$ is finite. Inverse image preserves limits for a locally closed immersion and for restriction to a pro-etale object, by the two limit-preservation lemmas. Limits of ring sheaves have their operations componentwise on the underlying limits, so these identifications induce a ring isomorphism $c_u:u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$. Its $n$-th projection is exactly the pullback of $B_X\to R_n$ followed by the constant-ring identification. Thus this is the coefficient map specified in the statement. For a composite restriction the same assertion follows by composing these isomorphisms: their composites with every quotient projection agree.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1); Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), and its restriction argument.

proof.text: Write $F$ for module inverse image with scalars transported through $c_u$. For a locally closed immersion, the immersion lemma states that $F$ is additive, exact and preserves all small limits. For a pro-etale object $U\to X$, weakly etale localization identifies its site with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. Module restriction there is exact by the ringed-site restriction lemma, and is additive termwise. Limits of module sheaves are sectionwise, so evaluating the restricted limit at $V\to U$ gives the limit evaluated at that same object over $X$; hence restriction preserves all small limits. Transport along a ring isomorphism changes none of these properties. A composite of these functors remains additive, exact and countable-product preserving. In particular their termwise derived functors are the ordinary inverse images used here.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8 proof; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0E8K (lemma-restriction-K-flat), and sites-modules.tex Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits).

proof.text: Apply normalized strict reduction-tower pullback with $R_Y$ there equal to $B_X$, $R_X$ there equal to $B_Y$, and quotient algebra tower $Q_{Y,n}=R_n$. Its hypotheses hold by the coefficient isomorphism and exactness just proved. The pulled-back algebra tower is precisely $((A/I^n)_Y)_n$, because the isomorphism in step 1 respects every projection and quotient transition. The theorem gives an isomorphism of entire derived strict towers $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}(K_\bullet)\cong(FK)_\bullet$. Its evaluations give the displayed finite-reduction isomorphisms, and it identifies the strict augmentations from the constant towers. In particular this proves transition compatibility for the actual reduction maps, independently of choices of K-flat representatives.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); normalized augmented strict-tower assertion of the cited node.

proof.text: The normalization isomorphisms for two quotients $b\ge a$ are, by the adic datum, represented by $(x\otimes q)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(q)t$. The representative comparison in step 3 sends $F(x\otimes q)$ to $F(x)\otimes F(q)$. Applying these two maps in either order gives $F(x)\otimes q'_{b,a}(F(q))F(t)$, since the constant coefficient comparison respects multiplication and $q_{b,a}$. These are equal balanced maps of sheaf tensor complexes, so they agree after localization. This proves compatibility with normalization maps as well as with the quotient augmentations $x\mapsto x\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); explicit quotient-normalization formula in def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum.

proof.text: Countable products are exact in both $\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y)$, even when $Y$ is not Noetherian. Apply the exact-product-functor strict-limit theorem to $F$ from step 2. For the strict quotient tower it gives the canonical isomorphism $F(R\lim K_\bullet)\cong R\lim F^{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$. Compose with the derived limit of the tower isomorphism from step 3 to obtain $F(R\lim K_\bullet)\cong R\lim(FK)_\bullet$. This uses total derived inverse limit of strict towers, with its normalized Roos comparison, rather than selecting a completion of a triangle.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), especially Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); canonical exact-product comparison and augmentation clause of lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit.

proof.text: The strict-limit comparison also preserves maps induced by strict augmentations. Apply its augmentation clause to $\Delta K\to K_\bullet$, and then use the augmentation equation of step 3. It follows that the isomorphism of step 5 carries $F(\eta_K)$ to $\eta_{FK}$, with source exactly $FK$. Concretely, the signed Roos fiber has differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, and the unit has coordinates $((x\otimes1)_n,0)$. The comparison is the canonical product comparison on both coordinates; it therefore sends this unit to $((F(x)\otimes1)_n,0)$. These are the quotient completion units fixed in the constant-completion equivalence, so no unspecified isomorphism of endpoint objects is being used.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), normalized kernel inclusion in the proof; proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), with unit compatibility supplied by the cited statements.

proof.text: The constant-completion equivalence identifies the completed-coefficient Koszul completion with the strict quotient completion and respects their units. Hence the intrinsic condition of def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion is equivalent to invertibility of the quotient unit $\eta_K$, and the same equivalence applies on $Y$. Step 6 identifies its inverse image with $\eta_{FK}$. A functor carries an invertible map to an invertible map, which proves preservation of intrinsic completeness for each restriction and for their composites.

Fix the finite stratification and the chosen pro-etale covering families in the statement. If all covering-member restrictions of $K$ are intrinsically complete, step 7 identifies their quotient units as isomorphisms. Step 6 identifies these maps with the restrictions of the single morphism $\eta_K$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$. Noetherian stratum detection, applied with ring sheaf $R=B_X$, says that these exact inverse images jointly detect isomorphisms; thus $\eta_K$ is invertible. The constant-completion equivalence then gives intrinsic completeness of $K$. Conversely, apply the preservation already proved to every stratum and covering-member composite. This proves the equivalence for the specified arbitrary covering families.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication, completeness devissage; stratum detection via Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and 09AB (lemma-thickening).

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), and completeness devissage in Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication. Strict-tower and unit details follow Stacks Tags 03EL, 0941, 099M, 0A0E and the existing normalized strict-tower comparison statements.

lean.statement: theorem stratum_completion_unit_restriction (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X] (S : FiniteLocallyClosedStratification X) (V : ∀ i : Fin S.n, Scheme.Cover.{w} proetalePrecoverage (S.domain i)) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = d.ideal) (K : d.derived X) (C : CochainComplex (reductionModules X (d.completedRing X)) ℤ) (eC : DerivedCategory.Q.obj C ≅ K) : IsDerivedCompleteIntrinsic X d r a ha K C eC ↔ ∀ (i : Fin S.n) (j : (V i).I₀), ∀ (D : CochainComplex (reductionModules ((V i).X j) (d.completedRing ((V i).X j))) ℤ) (eD : DerivedCategory.Q.obj D ≅ (d.pull ((V i).f j ≫ S.immersion i)).obj K), IsDerivedCompleteIntrinsic ((V i).X j) d r a ha ((d.pull ((V i).f j ≫ S.immersion i)).obj K) D eD
lean.note: All clauses are rendered by the listed declarations: the canonical coefficient projection square and exact module restriction; normalized comparison of the actual strict reduction towers; finite evaluation and quotient-normalization equations; the constant/derived-limit mate and its invertibility for the specified restrictions; the actual quotient completion-unit equation; intrinsic preservation and detection by every chosen pro-etale cover of every finite locally closed stratum. The original statement is unchanged. IntrinsicCompletion supplies the existing canonical transport of the recorded intrinsic predicate to the actual continuous-function coefficient presentation. No arbitrary endpoint or cone comparison is chosen.
